channel.title: Negative-Safe Entity
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Negative-Safe Entity" - An entity that *wants* to be contained.

item.title: Re: Negative-Safe Entity
item.content:encoded:
Either way, at what point do I know if I can post a draft?

If you do not yet have a successful mainsite page, you need two greenlights on a concept before you can post a draft for critique in the Draft Critique forum. Reviewers will be very clear when they are giving a greenlight (and if you're uncertain, you can always ask to confirm).

If you would like to receive feedback on a draft without greenlights, you can ask for draft critique in the IRC chatrooms (though some reviewers may still request that you get the concept reviewed first).

item.title: Re: Negative-Safe Entity
item.content:encoded:
Now I'm thinking it should be Safe again… downsides of unusual containment I suppose. There is nothing theoretically stopping the entity from being destructive other than a lack of "powers" (the foundation instructs members to cooperate with the entity, but to "keep up the ruse" that they are being manipulated).

Perhaps once the draft is up the classification can be further debated.

Either way, at what point do I know if I can post a draft? Sorry for the noob question — this is my first attempt at writing an SCP.

item.title: Re: Negative-Safe Entity
item.content:encoded:
Second, I would call this Thaumiel instead of Safe. After all the Foundation’s using it to build cells for other SCPs.

I'm not entirely convinced this would be Thaumiel, since the entity itself isn't actively containing anything, it's just being a convenient builder. The Foundation could easily contain the same anomalies with structures built out of mundane items that fundamentally serve the same purpose.

It just hijacks resources (probably by impersonating personnel or hacking computers?) in order to have its cells created.

This would be a big red flag for me. Thaumiel anomalies by nature need to be trustworthy, and if this thing is "hijacking" resources via any sort of underhanded shenanigans, that makes it inherently untrustworthy and unreliable. Does the Foundation have any sort of control over its loyalty? Do they have any reassurance it won't spontaneously go rogue?

item.title: Re: Negative-Safe Entity
item.content:encoded:
Thank you, I agree it probably is Thaumiel, not Safe - good call. The draft I've already written is quite short.

As for its "powers" it somehow "sees" the future insofar as it creates cells to contain itself that are specifically tailored to some future SCP. It just hijacks resources (probably by impersonating personnel or hacking computers?) in order to have its cells created.

The references to other SCP's is just a quick call out to unique cells to "prove" that it somehow has precognition for what cells to construct.

item.title: Re: Negative-Safe Entity
item.content:encoded: sounds a lot like SCP-3101 to me. i like the idea of it trying to be contained. twist: what if when it does get contained it causes an event? what if its already global but needs to be contained by keeping it global, like a show that just wont die, and by containing it it has to be broadcasted to the public?

item.title: Re: Negative-Safe Entity
item.content:encoded: I have to say, I’m a big fan of creative containment, so you've already got me there. I have three main notes for this concept. First, I think you should be more specific as to what the properties of this anomaly are. Do they manifest cells around them and the resources go missing or do they steal the resources and actively build the cells? This isn’t that big of a deal, I just think it should be clear. Second, I would call this Thaumiel instead of Safe. After all the Foundation’s using it to build cells for other SCPs. The third is more of a recommendation for writing. I wouldn’t recommend making this too long of an article. You’re mentioning interviews and tying this into other SCPs and that’s all fine, I just want to make sure you aren’t going to be running on one idea the whole time. Because I like this concept and I think it’d make for an interesting article, but there isn’t much to say about it from what I’m seeing so make sure not to repeat yourself.

item.title: Negative-Safe Entity
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, Intrigue

Page Layout (Optional): Typical SCP article, including interview with the Dr that initially specified designation.

Elevator Pitch: Just a regular person that wants to be secured, contained, and protected.

Central Narrative: They are found having snuck into a containment cell for a Euclid class before it arrived.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: They keep hijacking foundation assets to produce containment cells for themselves, so they get an SCP article where there special rules are "get them out of the cell" since they make good cells quickly and cheaply relative to proper channels.

Additional Notes: Ties in with many other SCPs (by having their cells made by this entity), unique "history" for main entity.

Original Motivation: Originally thought of by imagining the "box" analogy. Many edge-cases are covered (e.g. thaumiel class), but what about if the entity would enter the box if not prevented? I pictured a gas that had to be expunged, but didn't find a good story there, eventually ended up with this. Still Safe class though.
